errors.quote: A form is nondegenerate when its Gram matrix (the matrix of pairings of basis vectors) is invertible, which is why dimensions must be finite.
errors.problem: Nondegeneracy (no nonzero vector orthogonal to the whole space) does not by itself require finite dimension; only the Gram-matrix criterion, and the splitting A = B ⊥ P for a nondegenerate subspace P, use finiteness. The causal clause is loose. The paper only works with finite-dimensional spaces (F = Q^h or F_2^h, lines 856-868) and gives no such reason.

errors.quote: The basis vectors $\mathbf b\otimes\mathbf g_j$ of $A\otimes C$ span $B\otimes C$
errors.problem: The page defined $\mathbf g_j$ as a basis of $G$, then uses it as a basis of $C$ without introducing it. A reader has to supply 'let $(\mathbf g_j)$ be a basis of $C$'. The argument itself is right.
